title: Prep: eval deep-dive for optimize AB regression
content:
Meeting goal: build a crisp hypothesis for the recent QA signal drop on the embedding+rerank pathway, decide immediate mitigation (rollback vs prompt fix) and concrete experiments for the next 48–72h.

Context / TL;DR:
- Last week’s staged rollout of quantized model v3-q8 for cost savings coincided with an observed drop in top-1 rerank accuracy (service metric: rerank_top1_correct_rate) from 92.1% -> 88.6% on canary traffic. Latency and throughput improved as expected.
- The Optimize eval harness shows regressions concentrated on long-context prompts (seq_len > 1024) and on a small set of prompt templates that rely on exact-match / structured outputs.
- A/B run snapshot: cohort A (v2 FP16) baseline; cohort B (v3-q8) new. Sample size ~12k queries over 48h from production-sampled prompts.

Data to have in the meeting (bring these):
- Priya: Can you bring the per-prompt confusion matrix CSV and the full list of 423 failing prompt ids (s3://optimize/evals/failures/jun14-16.csv)?
- Liam: latency and token-cost breakouts by model variant + sequence-length histogram for the AB window.
- Me (Noah): quick eval dashboard: Rouge-L / exact-match / rerank_top1 for the 10 most regressed prompt groups, and the AB test significance calc (bootstrap CI) I ran this morning.

Quick findings I already pulled (pre-meeting notes):
- Failure mode clusters:
  1) Structured extraction templates (fields in fixed order) — v3-q8 produces extra tokens leading to parse mismatches.
  2) Ambiguous instruction prompts (few-shot prompts with 2 examples) — output ordering inconsistent, ties broken differently.
  3) Long-context degradation — KV-cache behavior seems fine in logs but token-level token_distribution shows more repeated filler tokens for q8 variant.
- Metric correlations: most regressed prompts show lower normalized log-prob for the gold substring (avg delta -1.8 nats) and higher sampling variance.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Quantization (q8) changes logits for structured tokens causing off-by-one tokenization downstream -> parse fails.
- H2: New kernel selection for long seqs favors throughput but accidentally increases temperature-like effect (more entropy) causing ordering inconsistency.
- H3: The prompt rewrite step in the new routing path (trim+chunk) interacts with the prompt templates in a way that loses anchor tokens.

Quick checks we can do in-meeting (15–25 min):
- Signal repro: run 200 failing prompt ids against both variants with deterministic sampling (top-p=0.0 / temperature=0) and compare tokenized outputs and exact-match pass/fail. If deterministic reduces gap -> stochasticity hypothesis gains weight.
- Token-level diff: compare token ids for first 64 tokens across variants for a sample of 50 prompts to find off-by-one tokenization patterns.
- Prompt re-run with full-precision weights but q8 kernels disabled (if ops allow) to isolate quantization vs kernel/runtime decisions.

Decision tree for immediate mitigation (to present and vote):
- If token-level diffs show quant-induced token changes on structured templates -> rollback v3-q8 for production and schedule focused quantization re-eval.
- If stochasticity is root cause -> force deterministic inference for the affected prompt group (route to FP16 or set deterministic flag) while continuing q8 for non-affected traffic.
- If routing/prompt-trim bug -> patch routing logic and redeploy small canary (expected ~4–8h turnaround).

Experiment plan (48–72h) — concrete:
1) Deterministic re-run (owner: Noah) — run entire failing list (423 ids) with temperature=0, top-p=0; record new pass rate. Deliverable: CSV with before/after, due: 2026-06-19 EOD.
2) Token-diff sweep (owner: Priya) — sample 200 prompts from each failure cluster and produce token id diffs + histogram of token shifts. Deliverable: token-diffs.zip + short write-up, due: 2026-06-19 noon.
3) Kernel toggle AB (owner: Liam) — deploy a tiny canary that runs v3-q8 but forces FP16 kernels for the first 128 tokens; measure rerank_top1. Deliverable: AB dashboard link and pass/fail verdict, due: 2026-06-20 morning.
4) Prompt fallback policy (owner: Noah + Priya) — create a routing rule to route identified prompt templates to FP16 model variant until validated fix. Deliverable: rollout config and rollback playbook, due: 2026-06-20 EOD.

Notes for 1:1 with Priya after the review:
- Walk through the token-diff outputs together and decide whether to open a quant calibration ticket (RQ-quant).
- Discuss adding a unit test to the eval harness: deterministic token-level equality for structured templates to catch this early.

Open questions to resolve in the meeting:
- Are the failures concentrated by customer (PII/specialized domain) or spread widely? (Liam to confirm mapping to customer-id in AB logs)
- Is there a correlation between batch sizes used in canary runs and the regression magnitude? (Ops / release-engineering input)
- What thresholds do we want for automated rollback? Current: 3.0% absolute drop in rerank_top1 on canary with p < 0.01 — is that still the right policy?

Communication plan (if we choose rollback):
- Short incident note to #optimize-alerts (Priya to draft) with TL;DR, impact, mitigation, ETA for permanent fix.
- Postmortem stub created in Confluence with links to failing prompts, AB results, kernel configs (Noah).

Meeting agenda (30 min):
- 0:00–0:05 Quick context & timeline (Noah)
- 0:05–0:15 Data walkthrough: top regressed prompts and metric deltas (Priya)
- 0:15–0:25 Live checks: deterministic reruns / token diffs (privileged ops access required) (Liam + Priya)
- 0:25–0:30 Decide mitigation + assign owners (All)

Prep checklist for attendees:
- Link the failing prompt CSV in chat before start.
- Bring AB traffic histograms and customer-mapping exports.
- Ops: have a small canary rollback playbook ready in case we vote to rollback.
- Release-engineering: be available for kernel-toggle experiment (can take infra access).

Follow-ups (post-meeting):
- Noah: create incident/rollback playbook + confluence stub (due 6/20).
- Priya: token-diff report and candidate prompts for test-blocking checks (due 6/19).
- Liam: AB dashboard with kernel toggle numbers and cost/latency tradeoff summary (due 6/20).
- Ops: be on-call window for the canary run (TBD time block after meeting).

Misc scratch / notes-to-self:
- Remember to run the bootstrap significance again with stratified sampling (by prompt group) — current CI might be optimistic because of prompt group imbalance.
- If we rollback, capture a reproducible canary snapshot (inputs + model config + docker hash) to make repro easier.
- Consider adding a weekly regression smoke-test that runs structured extraction templates across quant variants.

End of doc.

Quick inline TODOs (one-line):
- [ ] Noah: start deterministic re-run (2026-06-18 morning)
- [ ] Priya: produce token diffs (2026-06-19 noon)
- [ ] Liam: schedule kernel-toggle canary + capture metrics (2026-06-20 morning)
- [ ] Ops: prepare rollback playbook (ASAP)
